title: Who Is God?
subtitle: A conversation about the nature of God

missionary.label: Missionary
missionary.sceneText: You are visiting homes in a quiet neighbourhood.
missionary.goal: Start a friendly conversation about God.

christian.label: Christian
christian.sceneText: You have returned from church and lunch with friends. Someone knocks at the door.
christian.goal: Respond thoughtfully to an unexpected visitor.

openingDialogue.script: Hi! We’re missionaries from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Do you have a few minutes to talk?
openingDialogue.listenerPrompt: Listen and respond naturally, as you would at your own door.

questions.prompt: We believe Heavenly Father, Jesus Christ, and the Holy Ghost are three separate beings. What do you believe about who God is?
questions.exampleAnswer: Historic Trinitarian Christianity teaches one God eternally existing as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, three distinct persons.

questions.prompt: If God is one, why does Jesus pray to the Father?
questions.exampleAnswer: The Son addresses the Father as a distinct person; Trinitarian belief does not say they are the same person.

questions.prompt: We believe Heavenly Father has a glorified body of flesh and bones. Do you believe God has always been God?
questions.exampleAnswer: The Bible teaches that God is eternal and does not change. He has always been God, and He is not a man.

questions.prompt: Doesn’t Genesis say we are made in God’s image? Doesn’t that mean God has a body like ours?
questions.exampleAnswer: Being made in God’s image points to qualities like reason, relationship, and moral responsibility. Jesus taught that God is spirit.

questions.prompt: We believe Jesus Christ is the Son of God and a separate being from the Father. How do you understand who Jesus is?
questions.exampleAnswer: Christians believe Jesus is the eternal Son, fully God and fully man. The Word was God from the beginning and became flesh.

questions.prompt: Didn’t Jesus say the Father is greater than He is?
questions.exampleAnswer: Jesus was speaking from the humble role He took on as a man. Philippians 2 says He shared God’s nature but took the form of a servant.

conclusion.closingPrompt: Thank you for talking with us. It was good to hear what you believe.
conclusion.reflectionPrompt: How would you explain the difference between the LDS Godhead and the Trinity?

sourceNotes: Opening, roles, and the nature-of-god and jesus-prays questions come from the webapp pivot brief. The always-god, image-of-god, is-jesus-god, and father-greater questions are placeholders added for review; confirm or replace them before changing status to published. The closing line is new in the six-step format and also needs review.
